title: Bench topology manifest, v0
description: One app's map: every step and every possible branch, so untaken branches render; plus, optionally, what the app can read (sources), what it can do (actions, never) and plain-language notes for Presentation mode. Registered by the app; the bench stores nothing app-specific. Edge vocabulary follows Open Agent Spec (ControlFlowEdge: from_node, from_branch, to_node). Keys starting with x- are free for an app's own extensions at the top level and on app, nodes, edges, panels, sources and actions; any other unknown key is rejected. See SPEC.md section 4.

privacy_note.description: What the app hides on this screen, in plain words. Presentation shows it instead of a generic line; it must not claim more than the app does.

track_record.description: The app's own claim about how it has performed, shown attributed to the app.

plain_label.description: The Presentation name, in plain words. Falls back to label, then id.

kind.description: Picks the icon and which details the node box shows. Default step. check: a node that guards the app (its Checks row).

description.description: What this step does, in plain words (the node's note).

actor.description: Who does this step. Default from kind: llm->ai, gate->person, check->rule, anything else->app.

moment.description: Replay's Play pauses here (a moment worth stopping on).

from_branch.description: The branch of `from` that selects this edge (Agent Spec from_branch). Matched against a decision event's data.branch; also drawn as the edge label.

description.description: What taking this branch means, in plain words; on an untaken edge, why it wasn't taken.

plain_label.description: Optional. The branch in Presentation's words; drawn as the edge label and the source box's "→" line there. Falls back to the target node's plain_label.

plain_title.description: Optional. The panel's heading in Presentation, in plain words (shown in the NOW card). Without it, Presentation shows the panel with no heading; title stays Engineering's name.

mode.description: latest: show the most recent matching event; append: list every matching event. Default latest.

fields.description: Declared panel: show only these data keys, in order, from the matching events. The raw view stays one click away.

story.description: Rendered by the app's story script (its panels[<id>] function). Falls back to fields, then the generic view, if the story has none.

audience.description: Which mode shows this panel. Default both. Presentation shows both and presentation panels; Engineering shows all.

sources.description: What the app can read: documents, tables, systems. Item text never lives here; it arrives only in retrieval hits.

kind.description: Open set, e.g. documents, database, api, inbox, message.

description.description: The app's own statement of what this is and what it can't see; shown attributed to the app.

count.description: How many items the source holds, when items are not listed (or not all are).

id.description: Matches retrieval hits[].id, check_result evidence and decision cited.

actions.description: What the app can do in the world (tool calls, writes).

never.description: What the app can never do, in plain words; shown as the app's statement.

node_from.description: OTLP apps only: how a span maps to a node.

story.description: The app registers a story script with its map (custom panels and renderers). See SPEC.md section 5.

check_words.description: Optional. A check's own words for its states, keyed by the check's name (check_result data.name) or a check node's id: {"passed": "Didn't trigger", "failed": "Triggered: sent to a person"}. Shown everywhere that check's state is (the Checks row, the NOW card, the node box). A state left out falls back to Passed / Didn't pass / Not needed this time.
